problem.title: By the time the customer picks up the phone, the car is still on the lift
problem.description: Extra work is the most nerve-wracking moment of any repair. Without a shared system it goes like this:

phone.title: Phone calls mid-repair
phone.text: The mechanic finds a fault, the office calls the customer, the customer does not answer. The information travels by word of mouth or on a slip of paper.

wait.title: Endless waiting
wait.text: Work on the car stops until someone replies. The mechanic loses time and the customer does not know what they are waiting for.

dispute.title: A price dispute after the fact
dispute.text: At pickup comes the question “why so much?”. Nobody has a record of what the customer heard and agreed to.

promises.title: Fewer calls, fewer questions, one shared picture

approvals.title: No more calls about extra work
approvals.text: The mechanic reports a fault with a photo, the office prices it, the customer gets a link and decides on each item. The decision is recorded together with the content, time and IP address.

status.title: No more “is it ready yet?”
status.text: The customer has a repair status page that opens from a link, with no login and nothing to install. They get a message at intake and when the car is ready for pickup.

team.title: The whole team sees the same thing
team.text: The mechanic works on a phone, the office gets ready information to price, and the owner sees on the dashboard what needs attention and how the month is going.

story.title: One repair from A to Z
story.label: Animated walkthrough of one repair in nine steps
story.note: Data on the screens is sample data.

intake.title: Intake in minutes
intake.text: You pick the customer and vehicle, describe the scope, list the tasks and tick “Notify customer”. The order gets a number like ZL/year/no., numbered separately for each workshop.

status.title: The customer has a link before leaving the workshop
status.text: An SMS or push plus an e-mail with a link to the status page. No login, no app, no prices. The customer sees the repair stage and the pickup date.

work.title: The mechanic sees their tasks
work.text: A “My tasks” screen, big buttons and a time tracker: Start, Pause, Finish. One timer at a time, and the time is counted by the database clock.

finding.title: A fault? Photo, urgency, send
finding.text: The mechanic reports a need: a part or extra work, urgency (urgent, recommended, can wait) and a photo. They can hold the task until the customer decides. Instead of phoning the office, they send a report.

quote.title: The office prices it once
quote.text: The bell, the “Needs” screen, net parts and labour, the VAT rate, a gross result. Extra work without a price cannot be sent to the customer. The link goes by SMS, by e-mail, or you hand it over in person.

consent.title: The customer decides on every item
consent.text: They see the photo and gross price, choose “Approve” or “Not now” and tick consent to the total amount. No login, on their own phone.
consent.proof: We record the content and its SHA-256 hash, the decision, the time and the IP address.

effect.title: The consequences happen on their own
effect.text: The item goes into the estimate, the work becomes a new task, the paused task returns to the mechanic and the order goes back to “In progress”. Nobody retypes anything.
effect.proof: An audit log entry that cannot be changed.

pickup.title: Car ready, the customer knows at once
pickup.text: Changing the status to “Ready for pickup” opens the “Change status and notify” dialog. The customer gets a message and the status page shows “Your vehicle is waiting for pickup” with the address. At pickup you close the order with the receipt number.

results.title: The owner sees the results
results.text: The dashboard shows what needs attention and who is working on what. “Monthly results” shows the share of approved extra work and the share of approvals made through the link: one number that tells you whether approvals work.

roles.title: Everyone sees their own screen
roles.description: The dashboard and permissions match the role. This is a rule in the code: the server does not calculate or send what a role has no access to.
roles.solo: A solo mechanic? One account, many workplaces: your own micro-organisation and membership of other workshops, with a workshop switcher.

install.q: Do customers have to install an app?
install.a: No. Everything works from a link in an SMS or e-mail: approval of work and repair status. The app is only for the team and also runs in a browser.

writing.q: Mechanics do not like typing. Will this work?
writing.a: A report is a photo, a choice of urgency and one click. The buttons are big and the screen is built for a phone.

invoices.a: Today we record the receipt number and date from your cash register. You issue invoices in your own software. An integration with Fakturownia (KSeF) is planned. Napiko does not replace a fiscal cash register.

program.a: Napiko works alongside it and handles communication and approvals. Importing customers from a file is planned, integrations with other software come later.

sms.q: Will SMS messages cost me a lot?
sms.a: We send SMS only for key events. The customer can turn on notifications on their phone and then gets the message at no SMS cost. If notifications stop working, the system sends an SMS itself.

noreply.q: What if the customer does not reply?
noreply.a: The link has an expiry (1 to 14 days). When it passes, you get a notification and see the case under “Needs attention”. You can send a new link or record a decision given by phone.

legal.q: Is the customer's consent valid in court?
legal.a: We record the content shown to the customer, its hash, the decisions, the consent to the amount, the time and the IP address. Napiko does not give legal advice, so a lawyer should assess whether such consent works under your contract with the customer.

offline.a: No, it needs a connection. Working without signal (a photo queue) is planned.

price.a: Pricing is still being worked out, so we do not quote amounts yet. You can create an account now and try Napiko in your own workshop.

story.label: Animated walkthrough of a repair through the customer's eyes in eight steps

arrive.title: You leave the car and get a link on your phone
arrive.text: At intake the workshop sends you a message with a link to the repair status. You tap the link and that is it: no login and nothing to install.

status.title: You see which stage the repair is at
status.text: Received, in repair, ready for pickup, collected, with dates and work progress (“2 of 3”). There is also the planned pickup date and the workshop's contact details. No prices and no internal notes.

alert.title: The mechanic found a fault? You get a notification
alert.text: When the workshop needs your decision it sends a message, and on the status page you see: “The workshop is waiting for your decision”.

decision.title: You decide, seeing the photo and the price
decision.text: Each item has a photo, a description, urgency and a gross price split into parts and labour. You choose “Approve” or “Not now”, tick consent to the total amount and send your decision.

sent.title: The workshop gets your decision
sent.text: You see a confirmation and a summary. The workshop records your decision: the content, the price, the time and the IP address. If you choose “Not now”, the workshop does only the original scope.

push.title: Notifications without SMS
push.text: On the status page you can turn on notifications on this phone, with no app to install. You can also switch off SMS and e-mail in one click. On an iPhone this needs the page added to the home screen.

ready.title: Car ready? You know at once
ready.text: You get a message and the status page shows “Your vehicle is waiting for pickup” with the workshop's address and a “Call” button. You come when the car is ready.

done.title: Pickup and beyond
done.text: After pickup the status changes to “Collected” and the link keeps working for another 30 days. A customer account with your vehicle's repair history does not exist yet; it is planned.

noAccount.title: No account, no app
noAccount.text: The link works in your phone's browser. You create no account and install nothing.

privacy.title: Prices only where you decide
privacy.text: The status page shows no prices or workshop notes. You see prices when you are asked for a decision.

masked.title: Masked contact details
masked.text: Your phone number and e-mail on the status page are partly hidden.

expiry.title: The link expires
expiry.text: A request for a decision is valid for 1 to 14 days. After that the workshop will reach you another way or send a new link.

optout.title: You switch notifications off yourself
optout.text: You opt out of SMS and e-mail in one click on the status page.

token.title: A link only for you
token.text: The address contains a long random token and stays out of search engines.

install.q: Do I have to install an app?
install.a: No. Everything works from a link in your phone's browser.

account.a: No. The link from the workshop is enough to see the repair status and make a decision.

refuse.q: What if I do not agree to extra work?
refuse.a: You choose “Not now”. The workshop learns of the decision and does only the original scope.

silence.q: What if I do not reply?
silence.a: The request has an expiry. When it passes, the workshop is told and can contact you or send a new link.

data.a: The workshop repairing your vehicle. It is the controller of your data. The mechanic does not see your contact details or prices.

sms.q: Can I switch off SMS messages?
sms.a: Yes. On the status page you switch off SMS and e-mail or turn on notifications on your phone.

seo.title: Security at Napiko – data isolation, audit log, customer links
seo.description: Workshop data isolation enforced in the database, an immutable audit log, data minimisation and secure customer links. What works today and what is being prepared.

hero.title: Workshop data and customer consents under control
hero.lead: Data isolation is enforced in the database, the change history is immutable and a mechanic sees only what they need for the job. Below we describe what works today and what is still being prepared.

isolation.title: Workshop isolation in the database
isolation.text: Every table carries a workshop identifier and the database enforces isolation (Row Level Security with FORCE). A forgotten filter in the code returns an empty result, not a leak. A test checks this automatically for every table.

integrity.title: Data integrity
integrity.text: Composite foreign keys do not allow linking a vehicle, order, task or file from another workshop.

audit.title: An audit log like a chain
audit.text: Entries are immutable and each contains the hash of the previous one. A mechanism that stores the chain head outside the database is in the app and works once production storage is configured.

minimal.title: Data minimisation
minimal.text: Mechanics do not see contact details or prices. The status page shows no prices and masks contact data. Photos lose location data before upload, and notifications carry no contact details.

links.title: Secure customer links
links.text: Tokens have 192 bits of randomness and only their hash is stored. Pages are excluded from indexing, sent without a Referer header and not cached. Public endpoints are rate-limited.

queue.title: Notifications that do not get lost
queue.text: SMS and e-mail go through a queue with retries, and a gateway outage does not block work. A notification is created in the same transaction as the data change.

plan.title: Honestly: what is not there yet
plan.description: Napiko is at an early stage. Before we start a pilot in the first workshops, we are closing the formal and deployment matters.
plan.label: In preparation

gdpr.title: GDPR
gdpr.text: Napiko is designed with GDPR in mind: the workshop is the data controller and Napiko the processor. The data processing agreement, terms of service and privacy policy are in preparation.

hosting.title: EU hosting, backups, monitoring
hosting.text: Planned for the production deployment. Until then we make no claims about where data is located.

data.title: Export and deletion of customer data, retention rules

other.q: Will another workshop see my data?
other.a: No. Isolation is enforced in the database, not just in the interface.

where.a: EU hosting is planned for the production deployment. Until then we make no claims about where data is located.

legal.q: Is the customer's consent legally valid?
legal.a: We record facts: the content, the decision, the consent to the amount, the time and the IP address. Napiko does not give legal advice, and a lawyer should assess the form of consent.

gdpr.a: It is designed with GDPR in mind (data minimisation, isolation, an audit log). The formal documents, including the processing agreement, are in preparation, so we do not claim full compliance yet.

mechanic.a: The customer's name, the vehicle, the registration number and the VIN. They do not see contact details, prices, the estimate or the office's notes.
